name: Formosa
description: A star 136 parsecs away, 9.7 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: radius 9.726 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 45.227 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.097) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: effective temperature 4803 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.132)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.86 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 7 published values span log g 2.39 to 2.858, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: distance 135.938 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.082), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 136 parsecs away, 9.7 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 45 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,803 K, so 9.726 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 56508: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 100655
quotes.card: HD 100655, also named Formosa, is a star in the zodiac constellation of Leo, located 451 light-years away from the Sun.
quotes.introduction: It has an apparent visual magnitude of +6.45, which makes it a challenge to see with the naked eye under ideal viewing conditions.
